Title: 3 Everyday Foods Linked to Faster Memory Decline, According to a 2026 Study

Description:
Blanking on why you walked into a room, or losing your train of thought mid-sentence? A 2026 federally funded Tufts University study tracked over 10,000 adults for eight years and points to three everyday foods: ultra-processed snacks, processed meat, and sugary drinks.

People over 50 getting a fifth of their daily calories from ultra-processed foods like packaged snacks and frozen meals showed cognitive decline about 35% faster. A separate 2025 study found eating processed meat daily, even just two strips of bacon, raised dementia risk 13%, adding roughly 1.6 years of cognitive aging per additional daily serving. And Boston University's Framingham Heart Study found drinking more than two sugary drinks a day matched memory scores 11 years older, plus a smaller hippocampus.

Small swaps help: nuts or berries instead of chips, chicken or fish instead of bacon or deli meat, sparkling water instead of soda.
